:::{#thm-ems-one-way}
#### Expected mean squares in the one-way random-effects model

Under @def-one-way-re:

$$
\ba
\E{\text{MSE}} &= \sigma^2
\\
\E{\text{MSA}} &= m\sigma_\alpha^2 + \sigma^2
\ea
$$ {#eq-ems-one-way}
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

This proof uses the fact that the
[sample variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/exploratory-descriptive.html#def-sample-variance)
of independent, identically distributed observations
is unbiased for their variance,
[the law of iterated expectations](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-lie),
and [the variance of a linear combination](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-var-lincom).

**Within groups.**
Given $\alpha_i$, the observations $Y_{i1}, \ldots, Y_{im}$
are independent with common variance $\sigma^2$,
so their sample variance
$s_i^2 \eqdef \frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{j=1}^m (Y_{ij} - \bar{Y}_{i\cdot})^2$
satisfies $\E{s_i^2 \mid \alpha_i} = \sigma^2$.
By the law of iterated expectations, $\E{s_i^2} = \sigma^2$.
Then

$$
\ba
\E{\text{MSE}}
&= \E{\frac{1}{a}\sum_{i=1}^a s_i^2}
&& \text{(MSE is the average of the } s_i^2\text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{a}\sum_{i=1}^a \E{s_i^2}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{a}\sum_{i=1}^a \sigma^2
&& \text{(each } s_i^2 \text{ is unbiased)}
\\
&= \sigma^2
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-ems-mse-proof}

**Between groups.**
Each group mean is $\bar{Y}_{i\cdot} = \mu + \alpha_i + \bar{\epsilon}_{i\cdot}$,
where $\bar{\epsilon}_{i\cdot} \eqdef \frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=1}^m \epsilon_{ij}$.
The group means are independent and identically distributed across groups, with

$$
\ba
\Var{\bar{Y}_{i\cdot}}
&= \Var{\alpha_i} + \Var{\bar{\epsilon}_{i\cdot}}
&& \text{(variance of a sum of independent terms)}
\\
&= \sigma_\alpha^2 + \frac{1}{m^2}\sum_{j=1}^m \Var{\epsilon_{ij}}
&& \text{(variance of a linear combination)}
\\
&= \sigma_\alpha^2 + \frac{\sigma^2}{m}
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-ems-var-group-mean}

$\text{MSA}$ is $m$ times the sample variance of $\bar{Y}_{1\cdot}, \ldots, \bar{Y}_{a\cdot}$,
so

$$
\ba
\E{\text{MSA}}
&= m \cdot \Var{\bar{Y}_{i\cdot}}
&& \text{(sample variance is unbiased)}
\\
&= m\paren{\sigma_\alpha^2 + \frac{\sigma^2}{m}}
&& \text{(substitute)}
\\
&= m\sigma_\alpha^2 + \sigma^2
&& \text{(distribute)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-ems-msa-proof}
:::
